docRequirement: `settings.md` binds the sandbox path controls to four keys NESTED under `sandbox.filesystem`: `filesystem.allowWrite` (:415, "Additional paths where sandboxed commands can write … Also merged with paths from `Edit(...)` allow permission rules"), `filesystem.denyWrite` (:416), `filesystem.denyRead` (:417) and `filesystem.allowRead` (:418), alongside `filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly` (:419) and `filesystem.disabled` (:420). The page shows the exact document at :460-:478 — `"sandbox": { "enabled": true, "autoAllowBashIfSandboxed": true, "excludedCommands": ["docker *"], "filesystem": { "allowWrite": ["/tmp/build", "~/.kube"], "denyRead": ["~/.aws/credentials"] }, "network": { … } }`. On top of the key names it binds a PATH-PREFIX contract at :444: "Paths in `filesystem.allowWrite`, `filesystem.denyWrite`, `filesystem.denyRead`, `filesystem.allowRead`, and `credentials.files` support these prefixes:" — `/` absolute, `~/` "Relative to home directory" (`~/.kube` becomes `$HOME/.kube`), `./` or no prefix "Relative to the project root for project settings, or to `~/.claude` for user settings", and :452 "The older `//path` prefix for absolute paths still works." :696 adds that these arrays concatenate-and-deduplicate across scopes rather than replace.
current: The write/deny path controls exist and are enforced, but under different key names, at a different nesting level, and with none of the documented prefixes. (1) `SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS` is `['disabled', 'allowRead', 'allowManagedReadPathsOnly']` — packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:183 — so only two of the doc's six `filesystem.*` keys are accepted nested. (2) The doc's other three path keys live FLAT at the top of the `sandbox` object under Nessy names in `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` (:172-180): `filesystem.allowWrite` is `additionalWritableRoots` (:64), `filesystem.denyWrite` is `deniedWriteRoots` (:62), `filesystem.denyRead` is `deniedReadRoots` (:51). (3) `filesystemSection` throws `invalid sandbox filesystem setting: ${key}` on any other nested key (:264-268), and `assertKnownKeys` throws `invalid sandbox setting: ${key}` on any other top-level key (:216-221); the tolerant managed path strips instead (:397 top level, :446 nested). (4) `filesystemRoots` (:303-316) refuses anything `!isAbsolute(entry)` with `sandbox-${key}-not-absolute` at :312, so no prefix but `/` resolves. Reproduced by running the real parser against the doc's own stanza (bun, this session): STRICT (user tier) THREW `invalid sandbox setting: enabled`; TOLERANT (managed tier) returned `{"excludedCommands":["docker *"],"filesystem":{},"network":{"deniedDomains":["uploads.github.com"],"allowedDomains":["github.com","*.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com"]}}` with SIX drops: `sandbox.enabled`, `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`, `sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets`, `sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding`, `sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite`, `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead` — all `stripped`. Prefix probe on the Nessy flat key: `~/.kube` -> `sandbox-additionalWritableRoots-not-absolute`, `./output` -> same, bare `output` -> same, `/tmp/build` -> ok, `//tmp/build` -> accepted but stored VERBATIM as `//tmp/build` (never normalized to `/tmp/build`). Same on the nested key: `.` (the doc's own `filesystem.allowRead` example) -> `sandbox-allowRead-not-absolute`. Scope reality: this fork composes exactly two sandbox layers, not the doc's user/project/local tiers — packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:69 calls `resolveSandboxSettings([...folded.layers, getUserSandboxSettings()], { floor: folded.floor })`. The user layer is Nessy's own `config.json` (`StoredConfig.sandbox`, packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:105), parsed strictly by `getUserSandboxSettings` (storage.ts:1293); the floor is the managed policy's `sandbox` key (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:243, :517, parsed tolerantly at :1358-1360). Nothing anywhere renames the doc's keys onto ours: `grep -ran allowWrite` over `packages`/`apps` source finds only prose in comments and the vendored upstream `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js`. The file itself names the divergence at sandbox-settings.ts:94-98 ("The other filesystem keys above are flat rather than nested under here, which is a shape divergence this key deliberately does NOT repeat"), and the parity audit records it parenthetically on row N10 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:728). Our own product docs publish the flat spelling: docs-site/content/reference/config/config-file.md:177 and the ru mirror :180 list `excludedCommands`, `deniedReadRoots`/`deniedWriteRoots`, `additionalWritableRoots`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands` — and omit `network` and `filesystem` entirely, so they are already stale against the code.
divergence: Two separable deltas, both on the settings-parse boundary; the enforcement half is correct and untouched. (a) KEY NAME AND NESTING. Three of the doc's four path keys are spelled differently and live one level up: `filesystem.allowWrite` -> `additionalWritableRoots`, `filesystem.denyWrite` -> `deniedWriteRoots`, `filesystem.denyRead` -> `deniedReadRoots`. The VALUES, the merge semantics and the enforcement are right — allowWrite/additionalWritableRoots grants and concatenates, the two deny lists restrict and ride the floor, and the resolved lists reach the OS profile correctly. Only the accepted spelling is wrong, which is why the fix is an accepted-alias widening and not a rewrite. `filesystem.allowRead` and `filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly` and `filesystem.disabled` are already correct, so the object is half-conformant, which is what makes the rejection surprising. (b) PATH PREFIXES. The sentence the finding quotes is about prefixes, and none of the three non-absolute prefixes is implemented for ANY of these keys, including the two whose names are already right: `~/` is not expanded, `./` and bare are not resolved against a scope root, and `//abs` is accepted but never normalized to `/abs`. So even a user who translates the key names by hand cannot write `~/.aws/credentials` or `.`, the doc's own examples. Consequence differs by tier and neither is an app failure: at USER scope the strict parse throws and `getUserSandboxSettings` (storage.ts:1293) catches it, logs "[settings] Invalid `sandbox` in the user config — the layer is rejected whole and ignored" (storage.ts:1239) and returns `{}` — the whole `sandbox` layer is inert while the rest of `config.json` applies; at MANAGED scope nothing throws and the tolerant sink strips PER KEY, so `excludedCommands` and `network` still apply while the write/read boundary silently disappears. Adjacent and out of this finding's scope but rejected by the same probe: `sandbox.enabled`, `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`, `sandbox.credentials` (:421-423), `network.allowUnixSockets` and `network.allowLocalBinding` are all unknown keys too.

change.symbol: SandboxFilesystemSettingsV1 / SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS / filesystemSection / parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1 / resolveSandboxSettings / filesystemRoots
change.what: Accept the documented nested spelling as canonical and keep the flat names as aliases (do NOT remove them — `foldSandboxRuleRoots` and `pi-agent.ts` both produce the flat shape internally, and on-disk configs already use it). Five edits. (1) Add `allowWrite?: readonly string[]`, `denyWrite?: readonly string[]`, `denyRead?: readonly string[]` to `SandboxFilesystemSettingsV1` (:103-152), each with the `settings.md:415`/`:416`/`:417` sentence, and mark the flat siblings at :51/:62/:64 as the pre-doc aliases. (2) Extend `SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS` (:183) to `['disabled','allowRead','allowManagedReadPathsOnly','allowWrite','denyWrite','denyRead']` — this one line alone stops the rejection. (3) In `filesystemSection` (:259-278) validate the three new lists with `filesystemRoots(section.allowWrite, 'allowWrite')` etc., so the strict tier keeps the same absolute/too-broad refusals. (4) In the tolerant branch of `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1` (:441-470) add three `toleratedList` calls with the right composition kind — `allowWrite` is `'grant'`, `denyWrite` and `denyRead` are `'restrict'` (getting this backwards inverts what a malformed entry does) — and carry them into the `filesystem = { … }` literal at :466-470 and the frozen projection at :484-494. (5) In `resolveSandboxSettings` (:542-609) fold nested into flat so `ResolvedSandboxSettings` keeps its field names and no consumer changes: the `granting` reader at :550-553 must read `[...layer.additionalWritableRoots ?? [], ...layer.filesystem?.allowWrite ?? []]` AND the floor-caps test `floor?.[key] !== undefined` must also fire on `floor.filesystem?.allowWrite`, otherwise an admin who writes the documented spelling loses the grant cap; `deniedReadRoots` (:604) and `deniedWriteRoots` (:605) must union `layer.filesystem?.denyRead` / `layer.filesystem?.denyWrite` into the same `concatDedupe`. (6) Prefixes: `filesystemRoots` (:303-316) must resolve BEFORE the two existing checks — strip a leading `//` to `/`, expand a leading `~/` against `homedir()`, resolve `./` and bare against a new optional scope root, then apply `isAbsolute` (:312) and the `dirname(entry) === entry` root refusal (:313) to the RESOLVED path and return the resolved list. That needs a scope-root parameter threaded down from `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1` as an optional `{ scopeRoot?: string }` option.

Pass the user scope root at :1293-1300 — `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1(layer, { scopeRoot: CONFIG_DIR })` — so a `./`-prefixed or bare entry resolves the way `settings.md:449` specifies for user settings (Claude's `~/.claude`; ours is the Nessy config dir). No change to the catch/report path (`reportRejectedUserSettingsLayer`, :1230-1241); once the keys are accepted the whole-layer rejection simply stops firing for a conforming document.

At :1358-1360 pass NO `scopeRoot`. A delivered managed policy document has no file on this machine to anchor to, so `./`/bare entries must be dropped through the existing `sink` with a named reason rather than resolved against a directory the administrator never wrote — the same posture audit row D3 settled for anchored permission rules. `~/` and `//` still resolve there, because both are machine-absolute.

Four: (a) the doc's stanza at settings.md:460-478 parses at both tiers with `filesystem.allowWrite` landing in `resolved.additionalWritableRoots` and `filesystem.denyRead` in `resolved.deniedReadRoots`; (b) the flat aliases still parse and the two spellings concat-dedupe rather than one replacing the other (settings.md:696); (c) the prefix table — `/tmp/build` unchanged, `~/.kube` -> `$HOME/.kube`, `./output` -> `<scopeRoot>/output`, bare `output` -> same, `//tmp/build` -> `/tmp/build`; (d) negative — a `~/`-only entry that resolves to `/` still fails `sandbox-<key>-too-broad`, proving the resolver runs before the guards and is not a way around them.

Add a case asserting `collectRejectedUserSettingsLayers()` returns NOTHING for the doc's `sandbox.filesystem` stanza (today it returns one row for `sandbox`), and keep one case that a genuinely unknown nested key still rejects the layer whole — the tier's strictness must not be widened by accident.

Rewrite the row to lead with the documented nested spelling (`filesystem.allowWrite` / `denyWrite` / `denyRead` / `allowRead` / `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` / `disabled`), name the flat forms as accepted aliases, and add the `network` sub-block and the path-prefix table — the row is already stale, listing neither `network` nor `filesystem`.

N10 closed the `filesystem.disabled` half and recorded this one only parenthetically at :728 ("our schema flattens the filesystem keys, so a flat key would still have rejected the exact document the doc shows"). Give the flattening its own row so it stops being a note inside a closed row, then regenerate with `python3 scripts/build-parity-report.py` and `python3 scripts/regenerate-deviation-register.py`.

blastRadius: Crosses BOTH a persistence and a delivered-policy wire boundary, so it is a risk trigger here. `SandboxSettingsV1` is the on-disk shape of `config.json`'s `sandbox` key (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:105) AND of the managed policy document's `sandbox` key (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:243, listed in the known-key roster at :517, parsed at :1358-1360). Widening the accepted keys is forward-compatible — every existing file still parses — but a config or managed document written in the NEW spelling is rejected by an older build (thrown and the whole `sandbox` layer dropped at user tier, stripped per key at managed tier), which is the release-ordering risk: a fleet must not receive a policy in the new spelling before the build that reads it. Direct readers of the resolved value, unchanged by this fix because `ResolvedSandboxSettings` (sandbox-settings.ts:188-196) keeps its field names: packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:57-69, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:3502, packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation-capabilities.ts:76. Enforcement is downstream of that and is NOT touched — packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/filesystem-isolation.ts renders `additionalWritableRoots` per backend at :133/:171 (seatbelt), :238/:275 (bwrap) and :327 (firejail); packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts:310-317. Internal producers of the FLAT shape that break if the aliases are removed rather than kept: `foldSandboxRuleRoots` and `sandboxRootsFromClaudeRules` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/sandbox-permission-rules.ts:145, :170-184) — this is the module that implements the same doc rows' "also merged with paths from `Edit(...)`/`Read(...)` permission rules" half — and packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:5213. Diagnostic surfaces that change what they print: `collectRejectedUserSettingsLayers` (storage.ts:1263) -> packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:275 -> packages/shared/src/config/config-doctor.ts:79/:467-475. Tests that assert current behaviour: packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/sandbox-settings.test.ts, sandbox-read-allowlist.test.ts, sandbox-filesystem-disabled.test.ts, user-settings-strict-report.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/sandbox-permission-rules.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/managed-sandbox-and-channel.test.ts:60, packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.test.ts:323. No renderer surface reads these keys — there is no sandbox filesystem editor in apps/electron/src/renderer (only IsolationNetworkPosture.tsx, which reads the network half).
userImpact: Concrete and reachable today. An administrator or user copies the sandbox stanza straight out of `settings-reference.md#sandbox`'s worked example (re-anchored 2026-08-29: `settings.md` SPLIT and the sandbox keys moved, so `settings.md:460-478` is dead at the PAGE level; the example still opens `"sandbox": { "enabled": true, "autoAllowBashIfSandboxed": true, …` with a `filesystem.allowWrite` list) into `~/.nessy-agent/config.json`. Nothing about the app fails, and nothing in the UI says anything: the strict parse throws on the FIRST unknown key (`enabled`), `getUserSandboxSettings` swallows it and prints one line to the process console — "[settings] Invalid `sandbox` in the user config — the layer is rejected whole and ignored: invalid sandbox setting: enabled" — and returns an empty layer. Every sandbox setting in that stanza is inert: the extra writable paths, the credential deny, the domain allowlist, all of it, while the rest of `config.json` keeps working normally so the file looks accepted. The same document delivered as MANAGED policy is worse because it degrades PARTIALLY: `excludedCommands` and the whole `network` block apply while `filesystem.allowWrite` and `filesystem.denyRead` are stripped as drops — the admin's write and read boundary vanishes and the policy still looks applied. And a user who correctly translates the key names by hand still cannot write the doc's own path examples: `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.kube`, `./output` and `.` are each refused with `sandbox-<key>-not-absolute`, so only fully absolute paths under Nessy-only key names work. The only place any of this is visible is `nessy doctor`'s rejected-layers section (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:275) and the startup console line — neither of which a desktop user sees.
